items.excerpt: 大人のクラシック入門にも大いにおすすめしたい一冊。ガイド前半の20曲には小学校の音楽鑑賞でお馴染みの曲が並び、続く20曲では、著者おすすめのバッハの崇高なヴァイオリン曲から、現代のゲーム音楽「ドラゴンクエスト」（!）まで、音楽史の要点を押さえたバラエティ豊かな選曲が楽しめる。解説には堅い専門用語が一切なく、平易な語り口で楽曲の特徴を的確に突いてゆく。各曲の作曲家欄や、別立てのコラムでクラシックの基礎知識を押さえている点も心にくい。さらに〈聴いてみよう♪〉欄のQRコードからすぐにYouTube音源へアクセスできるのもたいへん便利で、読んで・聴いて・学べる充実のガイドとなっている。

items.body: Label: Self released, 2026 Personnel - Jay Matharu: guitar, keys; Erik Brandell: tenor saxophone; Christine Lanusse: bass guitar; Jacob Johnson: drums. Jay Matharu is an eclectic British-born guitarist and composer living in Uppsala, Sweden. His bold sound reflects a strong connection to metal—he’s a member of the band Liv Sin—but Disillusion marks a turning point in his solo career, weaving prog-rock, fusion, jazz-funk, and R&B into a patchwork of influences shaped through carefully crafted arrangements. Each member of his quartet—tenor saxophonist Erik Brandell, bassist Christine Lanusse, and drummer Jacob Johnson—recorded the album’s eight original compositions remotely. The music emerged from Matharu’s Master’s research in Music Performance. “ Atrophy ” is introduced in waltz time by Matharu, who is soon joined by Brandell as the music pivots into a 4/4 funk excursion. Both musicians splash a multitude of colors across the fluid rhythmic tapestry before returning to the opening 3/4 meter. “ Bare ” keeps the ternary feel alive, aligning saxophone and guitar in stimulating parallel lines. Brandell’s solo, imbued with adventurous melody, eloquence, and energy, invites us into compelling jazz fusion territory. “ Cog ” reveals classical influences within a theme receptive to subtle tempo shifts. Johnson’s snappy drum fills carry a prog-rock attitude, pairing naturally with Lanusse’s popping bass grooves. The piece is fueled by Matharu’s chromatic runs in a thought-provoking meeting point between Joe Satriani and Rez Abbasi. The Indo-jazz-rock thread runs even deeper in “ Chalo ”, a kaleidoscopic mosaic unfolding through ten-beat cycles and paying tribute to Matharu’s late mentor, sitar player Pandit Sanjay Guha. While “ Deluge ” features a memorable theme, a touch of Latin elation, and the bandleader’s metal-inflected soloing, “ Butterflies ” is a rewarding odd-metered exercise driven by throbbing bass lines and strong melodic development. The blazing guitar solo unfolds over a septuple-meter backdrop before launching into a metal-jazz romp fueled with high-octane energy. Throughout the album, Matharu and his band periodically reinvigorate the proceedings, with the closing “ Bittersweet ” standing as another fine example of dramatic shifts in rhythm and mood, moving from R&B soulfulness to jazz-funk audacity while leaving ample room for the drummer to stretch out. Although the ideas on Disillusion emerged from improvisational exploration, the whole outshines the parts. Matharu is following a promising path. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Atrophy ► 02 - Bare ► 07 - Butterflies

items.body:
A decade into his career, TEN celebrated the milestone the best way he knows how — on stage. Across TEN:CORE0110, the Thai superstar's sold-out three-night residency transformed Thailand into the centre of his ever-growing universe, bringing together fans for a career-spanning spectacle that looked back on his journey while hinting at what comes next.

Opening with 'Nightwalker' — the track that signalled the beginning of his solo era — TEN wasted no time setting the tone. The performance flowed seamlessly into fan favourites including 'ON TEN', 'Birthday', and 'Shadow', each elevated by intricate choreography, cinematic visuals, and polished production that highlighted his reputation as one of pop's most dynamic performers.

The energy only climbed higher as grooves from 'Dangerous', 'Enough For Me', and 'Water' had the audience on their feet, before shifting into more emotional territory with 'New Heroes', 'Butterfly', and 'Lie With You'. By the time 'Bambola', 'Sweet As Sin', and 'STUNNER' arrived, TEN had delivered a set that showcased not only his versatility but also the artistic evolution that has defined his past ten years.

The residency became even more memorable thanks to surprise appearances from NuNew, PiXXiE, NONT TANONT, Jeff Satur, and PP Krit, each joining TEN on stage to celebrate the landmark occasion and turning the anniversary into a celebration shared with friends and collaborators.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by PiXXiE (@pixxie_official)

The biggest surprise, however, came on the final night. TEN unveiled 'If You Don't Mean It' live for the very first time, giving fans an exclusive preview ahead of its official global release on 27 July. As the concert reached its finale, one final reveal awaited the crowd: a cinematic teaser announcing 'OUTWEST', his upcoming English-language single slated for release in September.

More than a retrospective, TEN:CORE0110 felt like a statement of intent. While the residency celebrated the achievements that have established TEN as a global performer, it also made one thing clear — the next chapter is already underway, and he's stepping into it with the same ambition and artistry that have defined his first decade.

items.body: Label: Defkaz Records, 2026 Personnel - Ivo Perelman: tenor saxophone; Elliott Sharp: 8-string electric guitar; Cyro Baptista: percussion, vocals. Triacontagon unites intrepid saxophonist Ivo Perelman, experimental guitarist Elliott Sharp, and resourceful percussionist Cyro Baptista in a recording that seems inspired by the rainforest. Their highly structured free jazz is filled with mystery and misty sonic landscapes, and it’s refreshing to hear Perelman reconnecting with his Brazilian roots, embracing a cross-genre approach with a contemporary edge, aided by Sharp’s remarkable range of textural possibilities. On the opener, “ Dionysus in the Amazon ”, Sharp lays down snappy grooves in the lower register of his eight-string electric guitar while Baptista follows a ritualistic procession of rhythms that ranges from crisp rattles and bright metallic tinkles to deep, resonant vibrations. Perelman moves sinuously above them—employing shrills and trills, cyclical pirouettes, and urgent, punchy staccato attacks—further intensifying the dark, ominous atmosphere. He balances descriptive lyricism and provocative expression with complete authority. At times, however, the electro-acoustic flow is interrupted as quieter, electronics-infused soundscapes emerge. The highly atmospheric “ Sacred Geometry of the Tropics ” features rippling ambient guitar textures interacting with gong-like percussion, flute-like sonorities, vocals, whistles, and, at one point, an extended cymbal continuum. Breath-cycling saxophone motifs and piercing intervallic leaps dance freely, leading to animated crescendos. “ Inside a Broken Circle ” and “ Electric Bacchanalia ” share a similarly dark harmonic palette, making effective use of Sharp’s poignant textures, Perelman’s wailing saxophone, and Baptista’s rattling percussion, occasional melodica, and jaw harp drones. While “ Irregular Forms in Humid Space ” thrives on a weird beat, acute saxophone lines, and low-pitched percussion timbres—all ultimately bound together by exquisite guitar harmonies—“ Disordered Continuum ” sets heavy Brazilian rhythms against electronics-infused art-rock guitar and intense saxophone flurries. The trio allows itself to drift through hypnotic sonic forests, its rapport sustained by compelling episodic cycles that leave ample room for the imagination while unfolding with complete abandon. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Dionysus in the Amazon ► 03 - Inside a Broken Circle ► 04 - Electric Bacchanalia

items.body:
izna are hitting the road. The rising K-pop girl group have unveiled the first dates for their WHO DAT GIRL? concert tour, with six cities across Asia confirmed for the first leg. The tour will see the group perform in Seoul, Taipei, Manila, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Kuala Lumpur, with more stops set to be revealed soon.

Tour dates:

19–20 September — Olympic Hall, Olympic Park, Seoul

9 October — Zepp New Taipei, Taipei

17 October — EGM Hall, EVM Convention Center, Manila

24 October — MacPherson Stadium, Hong Kong

8 November — Capitol Theatre, Singapore

5 December — Zepp Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur

Formed through Mnet's survival program I-LAND 2 : N/a, izna debuted under WAKEONE Entertainment in November 2024. The six-member group—MAI, BANG JEE MIN, KOKO, RYU SA RANG, CHOI JUNG EUN, and JEONG SAE BI—have steadily built their global fanbase with releases including 'IZNA', 'SIGN', 'BEEP', 'Mamma Mia', and their latest mini-album, SET THE TEMPO.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Three Angles Production (@threeanglesproduction)

For Filipino fans, 'WHO DAT GIRL?' in Manila will take place at EGM Hall, EVM Convention Center on 17 October at 6 PM. Tickets will go on sale from 5 September via Tap Your Tickets, with prices ranging from PHP 5,500 to PHP 11,500. Concertgoers can also look forward to fan benefits, including a Hi-Bye session and an exclusive photocard set for all attendees, while VIP ticket holders and raffle winners will receive additional exclusive perks. The Manila stop is organized by Three Angles Production and co-organized by O.N worldwide.
